messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: reserved-gpu-pool 'resv-east-3' utilization 100% -> queue growth detected. Pager triggered to oncall.
sam (oncall): on it. seeing high queue depth on resv-east-3, autoscaler not adding nodes. paging eng-sre.
emily-sre: joining. metrics show sustained enqueue rate ~120 req/s, avg latency spiking to 6s, throttling events for reserved-tenants up 40%.
ajordan: which tenants impacted? any enterprise reservations?
alice: AcmeCorp and StellarHealth show errors in their dashboards (500s / 'capacity_throttled'). Non-enterprise bursty traffic from tenant-8473 coincides with spike.
sam (oncall): @alice can you confirm noisy tenant id and whether it's in same reservation group? If yes we can try eviction/migrate.
alice: tenant-8473 is on shared tenant overlay in the same physical resv pool (resv-east-3). They've started a heavy batch infer job around 03:10 UTC.
maya: autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts failing with API rate limit from cloud provider.
ops-bot: AUTOSCALER ERROR: 429 rate_limit_exceeded -> scale_out aborted (see /ops/logs/3099991234/autoscaler.log)
emily-sre: posting relevant snippet:

```
2026-03-15T03:12:05Z ERROR scale_out failed: 429 RateLimit
2026-03-15T03:12:05Z INFO current_gpus=48 target_gpus=60
2026-03-15T03:12:12Z ERROR scale_out failed: quota_exceeded
```

emily-sre: looks like cloud quota + rate limit. We can't provision more GPUs automatically.
sam (oncall): escalation plan: 1) throttle/migrate noisy tenant, 2) free up reserved capacity by evicting low-priority reservations, 3) manual capacity bump via infra-runbook if needed. Who can run tenant throttle? @alice
alice: I'll add a temporary reservation throttle for tenant-8473 now (10m window) and kick off a migration to burst-pool.
clair-cs: starting customer bridge with AcmeCorp and StellarHealth for transparency — they reported errors.
jordan: we should avoid evicting enterprise tenants. instead evict background/batch reservations first.
maya: current reservation allocation list: AcmeCorp (reserved 16 GPUs), StellarHealth (12 GPUs), other small reservations + shared. Evict candidates: nightly-batch-job (8 GPUs), analytics-temp (4 GPUs).
emily-sre: I'll run eviction for nightly-batch-job now (graceful drain). Command:

```
$ infractl reservations drain --id nightly-batch-job --grace 60
```

emily-sre: done. resources showing freed 8 GPUs, but queue still high.
ops-bot: POOL STATUS: resv-east-3 total_gpus=48 used=40 queued=120 throttled=35
sam (oncall): manual capacity bump: @maya can you check on a manual add of 4 GPUs to resv-east-3? If cloud quota allows.
maya: requesting manual approval from infra-leads, but we have quota limits. I'll open support ticket with provider; might take 20-30m.
alice: migration for tenant-8473 started to burst-pool; routing will fallback if latency exceeds SLO.
emily-sre: while provider responds, enable emergency fallback policy: route new requests from impacted enterprise tenants to compatible model variant on dedicated-secondary (lower throughput but preserves availability).
sam (oncall): good. @jordan prepare small comms update for customers: what happened, mitigation, ETA for full restore.
jordan: drafting: "We saw a reserved capacity exhaustion in resv-east-3 caused by a noisy tenant batch job plus autoscaler rate/quotas. We throttled the noisy job, drained non-critical reservations, and enabled fallback routing. Manual capacity request submitted. Monitoring closely."
clair-cs: AcmeCorp is on the bridge; they asked if we'll compensate for errors. I told them we're prioritizing their traffic and will follow up.
ops-bot: INCIDENT LOG: created incident #INC-20260315-732, bridge https://redwood.bridge/INC-20260315-732
emily-sre: monitoring KPIs: enqueue rate down 60% after throttle, 95th latency for enterprise tenants back to 1.2s, errors down to baseline.
maya: provider support responding: temporary soft quota bump granted +4 GPUs for 30m while they process request.
sam (oncall): good — apply manual add now.
maya: manual add complete. resv-east-3 total_gpus=52 used=42 queued=40. Throttles cleared for enterprise tenants.
alice: removing migration route for tenant-8473; letting them run in burst-pool but limited.
jordan: posting comms update to customers and internal status page now.
clair-cs: customers acknowledged. AcmeCorp requests a post-incident report and root cause. I'll coordinate.
emily-sre: follow-ups: 1) examine autoscaler retry/backoff behavior for rate limits, 2) add a preflight quota check before scale attempts, 3) consider hard caps per-tenant to prevent noisy neighbor in reserved pools.
sam (oncall): agreed. I'm handing off to emily-sre for postmortem and to clair-cs for customer comms. oncall->emily-sre.
emily-sre: taking postmortem. I'll add SLO regression tests and a new eval to detect noisy batch patterns.
incident-bot: Incident resolved: INC-20260315-732 -> status: mitigated. Duration ~00:45. Tags: reserved-pool, autoscaler, noisy-tenant, customer-impact.
